title: Object-Oriented Programming
summary: Model real things with classes and objects.

exercises.title: Dog Name
exercises.prompt: Create `class Dog` whose `__init__` stores `name`. Create `Dog("Rex")` and print its `name`.

exercises.title: Speak
exercises.prompt: Give `Dog` a `speak()` method returning `<name> says Woof!`. Print `Dog("Rex").speak()`.
hints: Methods take self as the first parameter.

exercises.title: Rectangle
exercises.prompt: Create `Rectangle(width, height)` with an `area()` method. Print `Rectangle(3, 4).area()`.

exercises.title: Counter
exercises.prompt: Create a `Counter` class starting at 0 with an `increment()` method. Increment three times and print `value`.

exercises.title: Bank Account
exercises.prompt: Create `BankAccount` with `balance` starting at 0 and `deposit(x)` / `withdraw(x)` methods. Deposit 200, withdraw 50, and print the balance.

exercises.title: __str__
exercises.prompt: Create `Point(x, y)` with a `__str__` that returns `(x, y)`. Print `Point(1, 2)` (expected `(1, 2)`).

exercises.title: Override
exercises.prompt: Create `Animal` with `speak()` returning `...` and `Dog(Animal)` overriding it to return `Woof`. Print `Animal().speak()` then `Dog().speak()` on separate lines.

exercises.title: super()
exercises.prompt: Create `Person(name)` and `Student(Person)` whose `__init__(name, school)` calls `super().__init__(name)`. For `Student("Asha", "Joy")` print `Asha Joy` (name then school).

exercises.title: Class Attribute
exercises.prompt: Create `Item` with a class attribute `count = 0` that increases every time an object is created (in `__init__`). Create 3 items and print `Item.count`.
exercises.solution:
class Item:
    count = 0

    def __init__(self):
        Item.count += 1

Item()
Item()
Item()
print(Item.count)

exercises.title: Shapes
exercises.prompt: Create `Square(side)` with `area()` and `Rectangle(w, h)` with `area()`. Put `Square(2)` and `Rectangle(3, 5)` in a list and print each area on its own line.
hints: Both classes have an area() method.

quiz.question: What is 'self'?
options: The object the method belongs to
quiz.explanation: self refers to the current object.
